correctness.rationale: Exact arrival-order union criterion, explicit pair-overlap bound and degree-sum averaging imply the uniform rare-event estimate. A structural mixed-set cardinality bound gives the moments; an exact two-event integral and maximal-biclique argument yield the 2-regular two-point law. A standalone program passed 392400 direct permutation comparisons across 270 graph instances. Analytic proof rather than finite evidence handles arbitrary size.

value.rationale: A nontrivial bounded-degree deletion theorem yields a universal variance asymptotic that remains macroscopic although the coverage-density perturbation vanishes and the occupied count equals n with high probability. The degree-two exact distribution is a natural complete family invariant under all admissible cycle decompositions, furnishing a sharp finite benchmark and explaining a rare-event failure mode of variance-based Gaussian heuristics.
